tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files in a directory, skipping dependency and build directories. Returns up to 500 files. Use sparingly - only when you need to see directory structure. For finding specific files, use find_files instead.
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Reads the contents of a file. Pass startLine and endLine to read only part of a large file; both are 1-indexed and inclusive. Reading a range is preferable to reading a whole large file when the relevant location is already known, for example from a grep match or an error message.
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

parameters.name: startLine
parameters.description: First line to read, 1-indexed and inclusive. Defaults to the start of the file.

parameters.name: endLine
parameters.description: Last line to read, 1-indexed and inclusive. Defaults to the end of the file.

tools.name: run_terminal
tools.description: Runs a terminal command in the current project. For commands that finish on their own (tests, builds, installs). Do not use for starting servers or long-running processes.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Timeout in seconds (default: 300). Command will be killed if it exceeds this time. Raise it for a build or test run expected to take longer.

tools.name: create_file
tools.description: Creates a new file with the provided content. Pass an empty string to create an empty file.
tools.gate: Pauses on a unified diff. Nothing is written until you approve it.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: File content. May be an empty string for an empty file.

tools.name: write_file
tools.gate: Pauses on a unified diff. Nothing is written until you approve it.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace text inside an existing file. oldText must match exactly one place in the file, or the edit is refused so the wrong occurrence is never changed.
tools.gate: Pauses on a unified diff. Nothing is written until you approve it.

parameters.name: oldText
parameters.description: Exact current text to replace, copied verbatim from read_file output. Include enough surrounding lines to match exactly one place in the file.

parameters.name: newText
parameters.description: Exact replacement text. Inserted literally; no substitution patterns are expanded.

parameters.name: replaceAll
parameters.description: Set to true only to deliberately change every non-overlapping occurrence, such as a rename. Omit it otherwise; omitting means the single unique occurrence.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Searches recursively for text in project files.
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

tools.name: run_tests
tools.description: Runs the project's test command. For quick test execution only - do not use to start servers.

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Finds files by name or partial filename, skipping dependency and build directories. Returns up to 200 matches. Use specific queries (e.g., 'websocket', 'config') rather than broad patterns (e.g., '.').
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

tools.name: glob
tools.description:
Search for files matching a glob pattern. Supports wildcards like *, **, ?, [abc], etc.
  
Examples:
- "*.ts" - All TypeScript files in current directory
- "**/*.test.ts" - All test files recursively
- "src/**/*.{ts,tsx}" - TypeScript/TSX files in src/
- "*.{js,json}" - JS and JSON files

Returns up to 100 matching file paths.
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: The glob pattern to match files against (e.g., '**/*.ts', 'src/**/*.json')

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, uses current working directory. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description:
Search the web for current information, documentation, or answers to questions.

Use this when you need:
- Current/up-to-date information (news, prices, versions, etc.)
- Documentation or API references
- Technical solutions or stack overflow answers
- Verify information that may have changed recently

Returns a list of relevant web pages with titles, URLs, and snippets.

Current year: 2026
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search query (e.g., 'latest nodejs version', 'how to use react hooks')

parameters.name: numResults
parameters.description: Number of search results to return (default: 5, max: 10)

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description:
Fetch and extract content from a specific URL.

Use this to:
- Read documentation pages
- Fetch article content
- Get data from specific web pages
- Read content found via web_search

Supports:
- HTML pages (converts to readable text)
- Plain text
- JSON data
- Markdown

Max response size: 5MB
Default timeout: 30 seconds
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The URL to fetch content from (must start with http:// or https://)

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description:
Ask the user questions to gather information needed to complete their request.

Use this when you need:
- Clarification on ambiguous requests
- Additional details or preferences
- User confirmation before proceeding
- Input that only the user can provide

You can ask multiple questions at once. Each question will be presented to the user,
and their answers will be returned to you.

Examples:
- "Which API endpoint should I modify?"
- "Do you want to use TypeScript or JavaScript?"
- "Should I update the tests as well?"
tools.gate: Stops the turn and waits for your answer.

parameters.name: questions
parameters.description: Array of questions to ask the user (e.g., ['What is the API key?', 'Which environment?'])

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description:
Records the task list for the work in progress, so the user can see what is done and what is left.

Send the complete list every time — it replaces the previous one rather than adding to it. Keep exactly one item in_progress, and mark an item completed as soon as it is finished rather than in a batch at the end.

Use it for work with several distinct steps, and for a plan the user has just approved. Skip it for a single-step change or a question: a one-item list tells the user nothing they did not already know.

This records intent only. It changes no files and runs nothing, so it is available while planning.
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Records what the agent intends; changes nothing.

parameters.name: todos
parameters.description: The complete task list, in the order the steps will be done. Replaces the previous list.

tools.name: repl
tools.description:
Runs code in an interpreter that stays alive between calls, so variables, imports and loaded data persist.

Use it instead of `run_terminal` with `python3 -c` or `node -e` whenever the work takes more than one step over the same data. Load a file, parse an archive or decode a video once, then keep querying what is already in memory — re-reading the same input on every call is the single most expensive habit available here.

State lasts for the current turn and is discarded when the turn ends.

python: the value of a trailing expression is printed, as in a notebook.
node: a top-level `var` persists between calls; `const` and `let` are scoped to the single call, so assign to `globalThis` for anything that must outlive it.

This runs real code. It can write files and shell out, and is subject to the same approval and plan-mode rules as run_terminal.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Source to evaluate in the session. May be several statements; it runs in the same namespace as previous calls.

parameters.name: restart
parameters.description: Discard the existing session and start an empty one before running this code. Use after leaving the interpreter in a bad state, not routinely — restarting throws away the loaded data that makes this tool worth using.

parameters.name: timeout
parameters.description: Seconds this evaluation may run (default: 120). Exceeding it discards the session and its variables.

tools.name: process_start
tools.description:
Starts a command in the background and returns immediately with an id.

Use it for anything that does not exit on its own — a development server, a watcher, a long build you want to follow. For a command that finishes and whose output you need, use run_terminal instead; it waits and returns the result in one call.

The process keeps running after this turn ends. Read what it has printed with process_output and end it with process_stop.

parameters.name: cwd
parameters.description: Directory to run it in. Defaults to the project root.

tools.name: process_output
tools.description: Returns what a background process has printed since the last time this was called for it, along with whether it is still running. Output already returned is not repeated.

tools.name: process_stop
tools.description: Stops a background process and returns any output it had not yet shown. Use it as soon as a process is no longer needed — one left running holds its port and its files.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description:
Shows you an image. Use it to look at a screenshot, a diagram, a rendered figure or a video frame rather than inferring their contents from pixel statistics.

The image arrives with the next message, so describe what you are looking for and then read what you actually see. To inspect a frame of a video, extract it to a file first (ffmpeg, or cv2 in the repl) and read that file.

Accepts PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP.
tools.gate: Runs without asking. Reads only; never changes the workspace.

commands.name: new
commands.description: Start a new conversation, keeping the current one

commands.name: sessions
commands.description: List saved conversations for this project

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Name the current conversation so it can be resumed by name

commands.name: branch
commands.description: Copy this conversation and continue in the copy

commands.name: models
commands.description: Show the active model and those available for this provider

commands.name: approval
commands.description: Choose how much runs without asking

approvalModes.label: Auto read-only
approvalModes.description: Run reads and tests; ask before anything writes

approvalModes.label: Auto workspace
approvalModes.description: Also write inside the workspace; ask to delete or touch the system

approvalModes.label: Full auto
approvalModes.description: Run everything without asking — no protection
